title: Tool
summary: An equippable item: lives in the Backpack, moves to the Character when equipped (welded to the hand via a part named 'Handle'), and fires Equipped/Unequipped/Activated events.

properties.name: RequiresHandle
properties.description: Default true: the tool needs a part named 'Handle' to be holdable. Set false for handle-less tools.

properties.name: CanBeDropped
properties.description: Whether players can drop it (backspace key).

properties.name: TextureId
properties.description: Icon shown in the backpack bar.

events.name: Equipped
events.description: Fires when a player equips the tool. Locally, mouse input objects can be obtained here.

events.name: Unequipped
events.description: Fires when unequipped (swapped away or dropped).

events.name: Activated
events.description: Fires on click/tap while equipped — the main 'use' hook.

details.heading: Lifecycle
details.body: Backpack (inventory) → Equipped (parented to Character, Handle welded) → Unequipped (back to Backpack). Tools from StarterPack clone into each player's Backpack at spawn.

details.heading: Scripts in tools
details.body: Scripts inside a Tool run while it exists; LocalScripts inside tools run when equipped. Server Scripts in tools handle authoritative behavior (damage), LocalScripts handle local feel (sounds, effects).

explanation.whatItIs: The 'holdable item' class: swords, wands, flashlights, phones. Roblox handles all the equip/unequip plumbing; you provide the Handle and the behavior.
explanation.whyItExists: Every game with items needs the same equip pipeline — backpack slot, hand weld, activate input. Tool packages it.
whenNotToUse: For passive cosmetics — those are usually just accessories welded to the character
For UI-driven inventories where you want full custom behavior (custom systems may bypass Tool entirely)
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
StarterPack ──spawn──▶ Backpack
                          │ equip (slot click)
                          ▼
                       Character
                  (Handle welded to hand)
Activated ──▶ your gameplay (swing, cast, use)
```
tips: The Handle MUST be named exactly 'Handle' (case matters)
Server Script in the tool = authoritative behavior; validate every Activated action
Use Tool.Enabled = false during cooldowns to block re-activation
commonMistakes: Handle misnamed ('handle', 'Grip') → tool equips but doesn't attach
All logic in a LocalScript → exploiters get free damage; keep authority server-side
Forgetting Activated requires the tool to be EQUIPPED — backpack clicks don't fire it

examples.title: Sword with server-side damage
examples.code:
-- Script inside the Tool (server-side authority)
local tool = script.Parent
local DAMAGE = 25
local canDamage = false

tool.Activated:Connect(function()
    canDamage = true
    task.delay(0.3, function() canDamage = false end)
end)

tool.Handle.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    if not canDamage then return end
    local humanoid = hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    local owner = tool.Parent and tool.Parent.Parent
    if humanoid and hit.Parent ~= owner then
        canDamage = false
        humanoid:TakeDamage(DAMAGE)
    end
end)
